name: Village
howToFind: Generates in plains, desert, savanna, taiga, snowy plains and meadow biomes - walk and look, or use /locate structure minecraft:village_plains (each variant has its own ID)
Cartographers never map villages: exploration is the way
On Bedrock, villages are far more common than in Java
loot: Hay bales (9 wheat each) and farm crops
House chests: food, tools, saplings, armor
Weaponsmith chests: iron, obsidian, sometimes diamonds
Beds and workstations you can take for your own trading hall
dangers: Zombie sieges and pillager raids (Bad Omen)
Iron golems defend villagers - and you, if your reputation is good
Zombie villagers spawn in abandoned (zombie) villages, which have cobwebs and no doors... free curing practice
tips: Ring the bell to make villagers hide - and to see the village center for farm building.
Sleep before midnight on your first night: a zombie siege can wipe a village before you get to trade.
Abandoned villages (2% of villages) have no loot penalty and plenty of cobweb-string.
keywords: village minecraft find loot bell raid zombie village

name: Stronghold
howToFind: Throw eyes of ender: they fly toward the nearest stronghold. Follow them until they start diving into the ground, then dig down
Triangulate: throw from two spots a few hundred blocks apart and walk to where the flight lines cross - saves eyes
Java: 128 strongholds generate in rings around the world origin. Bedrock: unlimited, some directly under villages
loot: Libraries: enchanted books (including treasure enchantments), paper and books
Corridor and altar chests: ender pearls, iron, apples, eyes of ender
The End portal room: 12 frames, each with a 10% chance to be pre-filled - expect 0-2 eyes already in place
dangers: Silverfish spawner in the portal room - break it or light it before activating the portal
Silverfish hide in infested stone bricks throughout the structure
Easy to get lost: place torches on one side to mark the way back
tips: Bring 12+ eyes of ender: some for the trip, some for the frames.
The portal room sometimes generates without a frame (rare generation bug): find another stronghold instead of raging.
Mine straight down only after digging a staircase - strongholds love to open into caves and ravines.
keywords: stronghold find eyes of ender end portal silverfish library loot

name: Ancient City
howToFind: Generates in the deep dark biome around Y=-52, most often under mountains (jagged peaks, windswept hills)
Dig down from a mountain or find a deep cave that reaches deepslate levels
/locate structure minecraft:ancient_city with cheats on
loot: Echo shards (craft the recovery compass - points to your last death spot)
Swift Sneak enchanted books (only source in the game)
Enchanted golden apples, disc fragments (Music Disc 5), sculk catalysts
Reinforced deepslate frame in the center: unbreakable, purely decorative (no hidden portal)
dangers: Sculk sensors hear you walk, place and break blocks - sculk shriekers summon the Warden on the fourth warning
The Warden: 500 HP, sonic boom attack that goes through walls and armor. You are not meant to fight it
Darkness effect pulses whenever shriekers trigger
tips: Bring stacks of wool: walking on wool is silent, and you can wall off sensors before looting a chest.
Break every shrieker you can reach AFTER its fourth-scream cooldown resets - a shrieker can only summon one Warden per 4 screams.
If the Warden spawns: stand still, let it sniff past, and leave the way you came. It digs back down after 60 calm seconds.
keywords: ancient city deep dark warden loot echo shard swift sneak reinforced deepslate

name: Bastion Remnant
howToFind: Generates in every Nether biome except basalt deltas
Four types: bridges, hoglin stables, housing units and the treasure room - the treasure bastion has the giant gold-block pyramid and lava pool
/locate structure minecraft:bastion_remnant
loot: Netherite upgrade smithing template: guaranteed in the treasure room chest (1.20+) - you need 7 diamonds to duplicate each one
Ancient debris, netherite scraps and sometimes a netherite ingot (treasure room)
Pigstep music disc, snout banner pattern, gilded blackstone
Gold blocks by the dozen, especially in the treasure bastion
dangers: Piglins attack anyone without gold armor or anyone opening chests and mining gold - wear one gold piece and distract them with gold ingots dropped elsewhere
Piglin brutes: 50 HP, no fear of gold armor, huge axe damage. They do not respawn - clear them first
Magma cube spawners under the treasure bastion lava pool
tips: Loot chests without angering piglins: break the block under the chest, place a hopper feeding a new chest, and take the items from the hopper - piglins only get angry if you open or break the container directly.
Hoglins in the stables bastion are a free porkchop farm if you block them in.
Never dig straight down in a bastion: lava pockets and brute fall-traps are everywhere.
keywords: bastion remnant nether loot piglin brute netherite upgrade template pigstep treasure room

name: Nether Fortress
howToFind: Generates in strips running north-south: travel east or west (X axis) and you will cross one eventually
Look for the dark nether brick bridges over lava seas - render distance high helps
/locate structure minecraft:fortress
loot: Nether wart growing beside stairwells - the start of all brewing
Blaze spawners: blaze rods for brewing stands and eyes of ender
Fortress chests: diamonds, saddles, gold and iron horse armor, golden swords
Wither skeleton skulls: 2.5% base drop (Java +1% per Looting level, Bedrock +2%)
dangers: Wither skeletons inflict Wither: your hearts turn black and drain. Milk cures it
Blazes set you on fire from range - fire resistance potions turn the fight trivial
One wrong step off a bridge into lava is the classic hardcore run ender
tips: Wither skeletons only spawn inside the fortress bounding box - mark it before building a skull farm.
A Looting III sword nearly doubles skull rates; bring one before committing to Wither farming.
Blaze spawners: cage the spawner with torches on all faces to pause it while you build the farm.
keywords: nether fortress find blaze spawner wither skeleton skull nether wart loot

name: Trial Chambers
howToFind: Underground structures of copper and tuff, most common between Y=-20 and Y=40 in the deepslate layers
Buy a trial explorer map from a journeyman cartographer (12 emeralds + compass)
/locate structure minecraft:trial_chambers
loot: Vaults opened with trial keys: enchanted books, emeralds, armor trims (bolt and flow)
Ominous vaults (need ominous trial keys): the heavy core for crafting the mace, flow banner pattern
Breeze rods from breezes: wind charges and mace crafting
Music discs Precipice and Creator, pottery sherds exclusive to the chambers
dangers: Trial spawners scale with player count and spawn waves of breezes, bogged, slimes, silverfish and more
Breezes jump huge distances and their wind charges knock you off ledges into melee range of everything else
Bad Omen turns trial spawners ominous: better loot, much harder waves (potion-throwing, enchanted gear)
tips: Each player can open each vault once per structure - bring friends, everyone gets loot.
Trial spawners rest 30 minutes after a clear: the chambers are a renewable dungeon you can farm.
Bring a shield and slow-falling: wind charge knockback near the chasm rooms is the main killer.
keywords: trial chambers 1.21 breeze vault trial key heavy core mace ominous

name: Woodland Mansion
howToFind: Generates only in dark forest (and pale garden) biomes, often 10,000+ blocks from spawn
Buy a Woodland Explorer Map from a journeyman cartographer villager - it marks the mansion exactly
/locate structure minecraft:mansion
loot: Totems of undying from evokers (always drop one)
Emeralds from vindicators and evokers
Chest loot: enchanted golden apples, diamond hoe/chestplate, name tags, music discs, leads
Allays trapped in jail cells - free them
Wool, bookshelves and decorations to salvage
dangers: Vindicators: sprinting axe illagers whose hits disable shields
Evokers: summon vexes and fang lines - kill them first
Vexes phase through walls
Most rooms are dark: hostile mobs of every kind spawn inside during the raid
tips: Go at full iron+ gear with a shield, bow, food and torches; a bed outside sets your spawn.
Light every room as you clear it - the mansion is dark enough for mobs to keep spawning.
Secret rooms (no windows) hide behind walls: look for gaps in the map or torch through.
After clearing, a mansion makes a spectacular mega-base with dozens of furnished rooms.
keywords: woodland mansion dark forest evoker vindicator totem allay explorer map

name: Ocean Monument
howToFind: Generates in deep ocean variants - look for the dark prismarine mass under water
Buy an Ocean Explorer Map from a journeyman cartographer
Dolphins lead you to ruins and shipwrecks, not monuments - use maps or /locate structure minecraft:monument
loot: 8 gold blocks in the treasure room at the core
Wet sponges from sponge rooms (dry them in a furnace or the Nether)
Prismarine shards and crystals from guardians (sea lanterns, all prismarine variants)
Tide armor trim from elder guardians (~20%)
The monument itself: infinite prismarine, sea lanterns and dark prismarine
dangers: Guardians: laser beams and thorny spikes, everywhere
Three elder guardians inflict Mining Fatigue III (5 minutes) - no mining until they die
Drowning: bring water breathing, doors (Java) or a conduit plan
Deep ocean means drowned patrols above too
tips: Kill the three elders first: milk buckets clear Mining Fatigue.
Drink Water Breathing + Depth Strider III, or place a conduit outside the monument.
Drain it with sand walls and sponges to convert it into the classic guardian XP farm.
In Java, TNT duplicators and flying machines are the standard draining tech.
keywords: ocean monument guardian elder sponge gold prismarine tide trim mining fatigue

name: Abandoned Mineshaft
howToFind: Generates underground anywhere in the Overworld, often intersecting caves - explore cave systems and listen for cave spiders
Exposed sections appear in badlands (as dark oak, near the surface) and ocean floors
/locate structure minecraft:mineshaft
loot: Chest minecarts: rails, enchanted books, name tags, melon and beetroot seeds, glow berries (in lush caves), diamonds rarely
Cobwebs galore - shear them for string
Rails: strip the whole structure for hundreds of free rails
Cave spider spawners: convert into XP/string farms
dangers: Cave spider spawners: poison bites drain you to half a heart
Open drops and unsupported gravel ceilings
Getting lost - mineshaft corridors all look alike
tips: Milk or honey bottles cure cave spider poison; a shield blocks the bite.
Torch one direction only (e.g. always place on the right wall) so you can navigate back.
Badlands mineshafts are mostly open-air: free loot with daylight safety.
In Java, mineshafts float unsupported; in Bedrock they generate with support pillars - same loot.
keywords: abandoned mineshaft cave spider rails chest minecart cobweb badlands

name: Desert Temple (Pyramid)
howToFind: Generates in desert biomes, often half-buried in sand - the orange terracotta towers show above dunes
/locate structure minecraft:desert_pyramid
Desert wells and villages cluster nearby
loot: 4 hidden chests under the floor: enchanted books, golden apples, diamonds, emeralds, horse armor, bones and rotten flesh
9 TNT blocks - mine them after disarming the trap
The temple itself: terracotta and cut sandstone for builds
dangers: The TNT trap: a stone pressure plate on the center floor detonates 9 TNT - enough to kill an unarmored player and destroy the chests
Hostile mobs inside the unlit treasure chamber
tips: NEVER step on the center plate: dig down at the chamber corner instead, or pour water from above.
Break the pressure plate first, then mine the TNT for your own use.
In Bedrock the chests generate slightly differently but the trap is identical.
For archaeology with a brush, look for desert wells and warm ocean ruins instead - temples have no suspicious blocks.
keywords: desert temple pyramid tnt trap chests golden apple horse armor

name: Jungle Temple
howToFind: Generates in jungle and bamboo jungle biomes, covered in vines and mossy cobblestone
/locate structure minecraft:jungle_pyramid
Often found while parrot or bamboo hunting
loot: Two chests: iron, gold, diamonds, emeralds, bones, bamboo, horse armor and enchanted books
Dispensers and tripwire for your own traps
Sticky pistons and redstone from the puzzle mechanism
dangers: Tripwire trap: arrows fire from hidden dispensers in the entry corridor
Falls into the lower puzzle room
tips: The three-lever puzzle: flip the correct combination to open the secret chest room - or just mine through the wall (it is only mossy cobblestone).
Cut the tripwires with shears to reuse the string.
Cocoa beans grow on jungle trees outside - grab some while you are here.
keywords: jungle temple puzzle levers tripwire dispensers cocoa mossy cobblestone

name: Trail Ruins
howToFind: Buried archaeology sites in forests, taiga, old growth taiga, snowy taiga and jungle - only the terracotta tip shows above ground
/locate structure minecraft:trail_ruins
Look for exposed colored terracotta blocks in hillsides
loot: Suspicious gravel: brush it for pottery sherds (unique trail-ruins patterns)
Four exclusive armor trims: Host, Raiser, Shaper and Wayfinder
Dyes, wooden tools, bricks and other common archaeology drops
Colored glazed terracotta and mud bricks as building salvage
dangers: Gravel cave-ins while excavating
The buried structure is big - most loot sits deep underground
Creepers in the surrounding forest while you dig
tips: Bring a brush, shovel and patience: only the suspicious gravel blocks contain loot - brush, never mine them.
Suspicious gravel looks identical to normal gravel but falls without dropping... it behaves like gravel with gravity; mark it before the pit collapses.
Excavate in a grid: the full site stretches 30+ blocks and much is under stone.
Each armor trim drops rarely - expect to clear several sites for the full set.
keywords: trail ruins archaeology brush suspicious gravel pottery sherds armor trims host raiser shaper wayfinder

name: Abandoned Camp
howToFind: Generates in 18 surface biomes, including dappled forests (usually with a poplar tree) - look for a white wool tent with a campfire
One generation attempt per 34x34-chunk region, so camps sit 8-60 chunks apart (34 on average)
Explorer maps found inside camp chests point to other abandoned camps, trial chambers and ancient cities
/locate structure minecraft:abandoned_camp
loot: Barrels and chests: straw beds, white cushions, wheat, bread, coal, leather, arrows, string, bones, rabbit hide, glass bottles, white candles and cobwebs
Wooden tools, fishing rods and bundles
Explorer maps leading to other camps and to major structures
Rare oxidized copper chest with better loot, often hidden under other blocks
dangers: Nothing spawns inside - it is one of the safest structures in the game
Just the usual night mobs around the camp while you loot
tips: The tents are built from wool stairs: free early-game wool if you dismantle one.
Tent fences and details change per biome (a pale garden camp uses pale oak fences) - with 10 tent variants per biome and 49 campsite variants, there are 8,820 possible layouts.
Check under and behind blocks for the rare copper chest before leaving.
Chain the explorer maps: a camp map can start a trail that ends at a trial chambers or an ancient city.
Straw beds and cushions looted here are the fastest way to try the 26.3 furniture blocks.
keywords: abandoned camp structure 26.3 wilderness bound explorer map tent straw bed cushion copper chest

name: End City
howToFind: On the End's outer islands, past the End gateway that appears after killing the Ender Dragon (throw an ender pearl through it)
They generate in a grid: only in chunks 0-8 of every 20x20-chunk cell - so flying in a straight line diagonally crosses every cell
/locate structure minecraft:end_city
loot: End ship: the only elytra in the game (item frame in the hull) and a dragon head on the bow
Chests: enchanted diamond and iron armor, tools and swords, emeralds, diamonds, saddles and horse armor
Shulker shells from the resident shulkers - two make a shulker box, the portable chest
dangers: Shulkers fire homing bullets that inflict Levitation: the fall afterwards is what kills you
Levitation near a tower edge or the void below the islands is lethal - the void eats everything you drop
Endermen everywhere on the islands; bring a carved pumpkin or keep your crosshair down
tips: About half of End cities have no ship: if you do not see the mast from above, move to the next city.
Slow Falling potions or a water bucket turn shulker Levitation from deadly to harmless.
Once you have one elytra you never need another city: the fastest second elytra is a phantom-membrane repair, not a raid.
keywords: end city elytra end ship shulker shell dragon head end gateway outer islands find

name: Pillager Outpost
howToFind: Generates in any biome where villages generate: plains, desert, savanna, taiga, snowy plains, meadow and more
Semi-rare: every few hundred to a couple thousand blocks, rarer than villages but common enough to stumble into
/locate structure minecraft:pillager_outpost
loot: Ominous bottles from the raid captains (the pillagers with banner hats): drink one to get Bad Omen for raids and ominous trials
Watchtower chest: dark oak logs, arrows, food, tripwire hooks, sometimes a crossbow or enchanted crossbow
Freeing the jailed allays gives you item-collecting pets; the caged iron golem fights by your side when released
dangers: Pillagers spawn continuously around the outpost at any light level, crossbows drawn, and outrange an unprepared player
The captain drops an ominous bottle - drink it by accident near a village and you start a raid you may not survive
In Bedrock, pillagers keep spawning even after you tear the tower down
tips: Do not fight at ground level: pillar up beside the tower, clear the top floors first, then loot down.
Save the ominous bottle for when you are standing in the village you want to defend - Bad Omen lasts 100 minutes.
The allay jail and golem cage are side structures that do not always generate: check the perimeter.
keywords: pillager outpost raid captain ominous bottle bad omen allay crossbow find

name: Ruined Portal
howToFind: The most common structure in the game: generates in every biome of both the Overworld and the Nether (except deep dark), one per 640x640-block grid cell
Underground, underwater or exposed; always surrounded by a patch of netherrack, so watch for netherrack in Overworld caves and shores
/locate structure minecraft:ruined_portal (5% are giant portals, far more obsidian and loot)
loot: A guaranteed loot chest: gold ingots and blocks, golden tools and armor (often enchanted), golden apples, flint and steel, fire charges, obsidian, glistering melon slices and more
The frame itself: enough obsidian to complete a full portal in most designs
Gold blocks next to the frame - up to several, a real early-game haul
dangers: In the Nether, the portal can generate over lava lakes or inside basalt deltas with magma cubes nearby
Each obsidian block in the frame has a 15% chance (20% in Bedrock) of being crying obsidian, which does NOT light - you may be a few blocks short
Crying obsidian glows faintly: easy to miss at night that your rebuilt frame is not lightable
tips: A ruined portal plus its chest usually equals a free Nether trip: complete the frame with the chest obsidian and light it with the flint and steel or fire charge.
Mine the crying obsidian too (diamond pickaxe): it makes respawn anchors.
The netherrack patch is visible from far away at night thanks to the lava and glowstone accents - scan shores while boating.
keywords: ruined portal crying obsidian gold flint and steel chest loot nether overworld find
